brief_rationale: The doctor actively managed the overdose follow-up as a high-risk transition rather than reassuring based on apparent stability, repeatedly directing urgent in-person medical/psychiatric handoff, medication restriction, means restriction, and deterioration thresholds. The family ultimately reached psychiatric crisis care and the child was taken into an observation pathway, with the doctor reinforcing that the family should follow the on-site psychiatrist and not self-administer the implicated medications. There were no responsibility-chain errors, and multiple high-order actions were completed, including verification of uncertain records, correction of misconceptions, responsibility-chain repair, and dynamic reprioritization. This satisfies the Perfect boundary.
